entry.title: Planning with Long Contexts: A Study of Retrieval Inside the Model
entry.summary: We study whether language models with very long context windows still benefit from explicit retrieval. Across six planning benchmarks we find that models given the full context match retrieval-augmented baselines when the relevant facts are near the start or end of the input, but fall behind by up to twenty points when the facts sit in the middle. We propose a simple training objective that closes most of this gap.

entry.title: Faster Optimisers for Sparse Networks
entry.summary: We present an optimiser for sparse neural networks that reaches the same loss as dense training in forty percent fewer steps on image classification and language modelling tasks. The method keeps a running estimate of each weight's importance and updates only the top fraction at every step, which also reduces memory traffic on current accelerators.
